concerns.text: FR-004 requires a 'frozen, small-scale LLM' to score responses but does not specify the exact model version or quantization level. 'e.g., Llama-3-8B' is a family, not a verifiable artifact. Without a specific model ID (e.g., 'meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct') and quantization method (e.g., 'INT4'), the scoring result is non-deterministic and cannot be reproduced or verified against the Constitution's Principle I.

FR-005 mandates a 'paired t-test' but the data structure (3 candidate responses per prompt) makes a standard paired t-test statistically ambiguous. It is unclear if the pairing is by prompt (averaging the 3 responses first) or by response instance. The requirement must specify the aggregation method (e.g., 'mean of 3 responses per prompt') to be verifiable.

SC-004 states the proxy model validity is measured by 'correlation >0.6' with gold standards. However, the spec does not define the size or composition of the 'small set of manually verified gold standard responses' required to calculate this correlation. A correlation of 0.6 on 3 samples is statistically meaningless; the sample size (N) for the validation set must be specified to make this criterion measurable.

The edge case regarding 'ambiguous prompts' states the system must 'flag these as low-confidence' but does not define the quantitative threshold for 'low-confidence' (e.g., 'if the scoring model's entropy > X' or 'if the score variance across 3 candidates > Y'). Without a numeric threshold, the exclusion logic is not verifiable.
